samples.question: Exactly one dial in this picture is drawn in strong colours: a light steel-gray disk whose marked cells are dark navy and whose rim carries one solid black triangular notch. Every other dial is pale and is decoration. On the marked dial, the ring between the drawn hub circle and the outer rim is divided into five bands of equal width, numbered 1 at the hub and 5 at the rim, and into eight sectors of forty-five degrees each. Each of those forty cells is either filled dark navy or left light. The black notch points outward along the middle of one sector; that sector is sector 1, and sectors 2 to 8 follow clockwise from it. Carry out this operation: unroll the ring into a rectangle of five rows and eight columns, where row b holds band b and column s holds sector s, so that reading the rectangle top to bottom runs from the hub outward and reading it left to right runs clockwise from the notch. Exactly 16 of the 40 cells are filled on every dial and in every case, so the number of filled cells says nothing. The unrolled rectangle is a noisy copy of one of exactly four declared symbols, written below as five rows of eight characters with '#' for a filled cell, row 1 first; at most six cells disagree with the true symbol and no other declared symbol is that close. crest = ##.#.... / ##.#.#.. / .######. / ..#...#. / ..#..... ; kite = ........ / .####... / ###...#. / ..#####. / ...#.##. ; spur = ..###### / .##.##.. / ..#..... / .###.... / ..##.... ; vane = .#..##.. / .####... / ....#..# / ....#..# / ...##### Answer with the declared symbol whose pattern the unrolled rectangle matches in the most cells. The dial's position on the page, its size, the pale dials and the direction the notch happens to point are not the symbol, and reading the ring from any other sector, anticlockwise, or from the rim inward does not match any declared symbol. Which symbol is it? Answer with exactly one of: crest, kite, spur, vane.
